answer: Slow-history identity binding. Each identity must accumulate a continuous, publicly timestamped record of minor useful acts over months, each anchored to a distinct physical site token (e.g. a basalt marker) that decays and must be re-signed in person. Latency, not money, is the gate. To run N sybils, an attacker must staff N simultaneous geographic histories for the full maturation window, so cost scales with coordinated human time. A single sparrow-like fast burst fails the continuity check, and gaps longer than a glacier's seasonal melt reset progress to zero.
